findings.evidence:
The acceptance criterion names the concrete default-slice shape: "A 6-document dual panel renders a v2 record; the same defect raised by both models appears twice with agreement: 2, and each entry is dispositioned separately." Every dual panel the Diff's tests actually render is smaller than the named shape — the largest is a four-document panel (two models × two lenses, no review-security doc):
```
+        out, _, _ = self.render_ok(
+            panel=[("review-contract", "qwen3.8-max", str(a_c)),
+                   ("review-adversary", "qwen3.8-max", str(a_a)),
+                   ("review-contract", "deepseek-v4-pro-0813", str(b_c)),
+                   ("review-adversary", "deepseek-v4-pro-0813", str(b_a))],
+            dispositions=str(self.write_dispositions([])))
```
No artifact in the package renders the six-document panel (three internal lenses × two models) that the acceptance criterion names and that the lane will actually run; the twin-agreement case is proven with two documents and the symmetry guard with four. The panel mechanics are size-agnostic in code (check_panel_symmetry iterates models), so this is an evidence gap, not an implementation defect.
findings.required_change: Add a suite artifact that renders the six-document dual panel (review-contract, review-adversary, review-security × two models) and asserts a review.record.v2 record with namespaced per-model finding ids, agreement: 2 on the twin pairs, and each twin entry dispositioned independently, matching the acceptance criterion's named shape.
